o1.biggest_strength: It focuses cash on the real risk: the top 5 matte shades, starts re-cartoning immediately, rejects the over-budget draft, and gives ops a dated action plan.
o1.biggest_mistake: It treats the held crushed-carton stock a bit inconsistently and creates a 1–8 Dec stockout gap that may not exist if the 3,900 top-5 held units are added to the 9,100 on hand.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Fix the held-stock assumption, recalculate the top-5 runout date, and tighten the palette clearance plan with a clearer sell-through target and channel owner.

o2.biggest_strength: The order quantities are tight, cash-aware, and well reasoned, with a useful pro pre-book idea for bridal artists.
o2.biggest_mistake: It says the top 5 still have only 2.4 weeks after re-cartoning, which misses the main warehouse fix and leads to an unnecessary back-order gap.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Correct the re-cartoning math, place all POs on Monday rather than some by Friday, and make the slow-stock plan more decisive for turning glitter inventory into cash.

reason: I would hand Output 1 to ops first because it is more complete as a Monday plan and stronger on slow-stock actions and customer messaging. Output 2 has slightly tighter math in places, but the stock-gap framing and less decisive clearance plan make it a little less ready.
